title: Reorganize routing policy and regional fallback logic to reduce tech debt
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Background: Over the past 18 months the routing layer has accreted multiple ad-hoc policies and fallbacks to address availability spikes, model variant mismatches, and regional capacity constraints. These changes were effective short-term but have produced brittle code paths, duplicated policy checks, and incorrect metric attribution during multi-region failover. This ticket reorganizes the routing policy code, extracts a single policy-evaluation engine, simplifies regional routing code paths, and harmonizes fallback logic for cross-region and model-variant failovers.

Goals:
- Replace scattered policy checks with a small, well-documented policy evaluation engine (policy DSL + evaluator).
- Consolidate fallback decision logic into a deterministic state machine to avoid duplicated heuristics.
- Clean up region selection code: isolate region-specific heuristics behind a thin adapter.
- Remove deprecated config flags and feature-gated legacy fallbacks.
- Add unit and integration tests to cover failure modes and rollbacks.
- Instrument detailed telemetry for policy decisions (decision_type, reason_code, eval_latency, input_tags).

Scope & Out-of-scope:
- In-scope: routing/runtime service (router-api and router-worker), policy config schemas, integration tests against staging clusters, small schema migration for policy configurations stored in PostgreSQL.
- Out-of-scope: client SDKs, billing/calculation code, infra-level autoscaler tuning; those will be coordinated but changed in follow-up tickets.

Approach / Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Design phase (week 1): draft policy evaluator API, simple DSL for common conditions (region capacity, latency budget, customer tier, pinned model). Document trade-offs on expressivity vs. eval cost.
2) Prototype: implement evaluator as a library packaged separately (router-policy-eval) and add feature-flag path in router-worker.
3) Migrate router-worker routing code to call policy-eval; run A/B tests in staging.
4) Replace legacy fallback logic with deterministic state machine (states: normal, degraded, partial-fallback, cross-region-fallback, emergency-fallback).
5) Add safety net: automatic revert if fallback-rate or error-rate exceed thresholds.
6) Rollout: Canary (5% traffic) -> Gradual ramp (25%, 50%, 100%) with automatic rollback knobs.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for policy DSL parsing and evaluation semantics.
- Integration tests that simulate region capacity loss and assert correct state transitions and metrics.
- Chaos tests in staging (bring down a region and validate cross-region fallbacks and cache invalidation).
- Perf microbenchmarks to ensure eval adds < 200us P95 to routing decision path.

Success criteria / Acceptance signals:
- Routing decision latency P95 overhead < 200us compared to baseline.
- Cross-region fallback correctness: for 10 simulated failures, chosen fallback target conforms to policy rules in 100% of runs.
- Reduction of duplicated policy code by > 80% across router repos.
- No customer-facing incidents during canary; rollout can proceed to 100% within 7 days.
- New telemetry fields ingested in observability (decision_type, reason_code) and dashboards created.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: policy evaluator mistakes cause unexpected routing. Mitigation: conservative default policy equal to existing behavior; feature-flagged rollout and automatic rollback triggers.
- Risk: eval latency regression. Mitigation: microbenchmarks, Caching of policy eval results keyed by request fingerprint for short TTLs.
- Risk: config migration errors. Mitigation: migration tooling with dry-run mode and manual review.

Operational notes:
- Add tracing spans named router.policy.eval and router.fallback.transition.
- Emit structured events to kafka topic infra.routing.decisions for offline auditing.
- Dashboard: Policy decisions by reason_code, per-region fallback counts, canary error rates + latency.

Backward compatibility:
- Policy config schema change will be additive. Router will accept legacy configs and translate them into the new DSL for a transitional period.

Deliverables:
- router-policy-eval library (Go) with README and DSL docs in Confluence.
- Router-worker changes behind feature flag.
- Integration test harness and chaos scripts.
- Migration script for policy configs and a verification playbook.
- Dashboards and alerts for new signals.
acceptance_criteria: Policy evaluator library published and dependency added to router-worker
Unit and integration tests added covering critical fallback scenarios
Canary rollout plan executed without customer-facing regressions
Decision telemetry (decision_type, reason_code) visible in dashboards
